title: The path `/tmp/jellyfin` has insufficient free space. Required: at least 2GB.
body:
### Description of the bug

The default /tmp size in Armbian is only 2GB, and Jellyfin stopped working after updating to the latest version.

### Reproduction steps

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hello,

I also had this problem with my Debian 13 VM. I added the following line to fstab (etc/fstab). It is important that the spelling is correct. Then I restarted and tmpfs was enlarged.

Hope this helps you.

```powershell
tmpfs  /tmp    tmpfs   defaults,noatime,mode=1777,size=4G 0 0
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: This is actually caused by a new protection mechanism we introduced to prevent corruption as a result of free space issues. 2GB is not a high barrier for hosting something as Jellyfin and I suggest increasing the /tmp in your scenario.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
What is `/tmp` used for by Jellyfin? If for transcoding, is there a way to move that to disk for low RAM devices? I actually thought this was the case already, like the cache dir used or so.
EDIT: Ah sorry, answered above. So same question for trickplay: If a feature requires above like 512 MiB of temporary files, I suggest to allow doing those on an editable path. `/tmp` is typically a tmpfs, which defaults to 512 MiB size (`mount` default). Jellyfin runs pretty well on low RAM devices as well, surely with limits regarding video resolution and stuff. But why introducing artificial hard limits if there are other ways?

`/var/log` requirements IMO should be left to admin responsibility: it depends on log level and rotation setup. 512 MiB is insane, and breaks RAM logging implementations. I mean even opening a log file of such size can cause practical issues with common editors.

<s>EDIT: I see the transcoding directory can be changed: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/installation/advanced/truenas#storage-settings
But I guess this does not affect the 2 GiB requirement for `/tmp/jellyfin` at the moment?</s> EDIT: For TrueNAS SCALE Jellyfin app only. They make this configurable for a reason 😉.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
I would suggest this change be rolled out in phases so people's installs don't just suddenly break and require checking the logs. Maybe start by displaying a warning in Jellyfin. Or as others have suggested allow alternate directories for tmp heavy features in Jellyfin.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I checked the code a bit: https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/MediaBrowser.Common/Configuration/IApplicationPaths.cs#L76-L80

> the folder path to the temp directory within the cache folder

and I remember that having `JELLYFIN_CACHE_DIR` on disk really was a topic our end for transcoding on lower RAM devices. This has changed in v10.10.0 it seems: https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/commit/c666f9d

`GetTempPath()` on Linux btw respects the `TMPDIR` variable. So one of these works around the issue on low RAM devices, moreless restoring the behavior of Jellyfin before v10.10.0:
```sh
TMPDIR="$JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR/tmp"
TMPDIR="$JELLYFIN_CACHE_DIR/tmp"
TMPDIR='/var/tmp'
```
`/var/tmp` typically is not a tmpfs, but more intended for boot-persistent temporary files. But varies by distro and admin setup of course. The `tmp` subdir when using data or cache dir is not needed, since Jellyfin internally uses a `jellyfin` subdir, assuring that there are no file collisions. But it is probably weird to have a `/var/cache/jellyfin/jellyfin` dir 😄.

EDIT: There is even a hint about this in the `/etc/default/jellyfin` env file:

> ```sh
> # temporary directory path; used to construct paths for short-lived temporary files
> # the old default was $JELLYFIN_CACHE_DIR/temp; use that to restore previous behaviour,
> # though it will have an additional jellyfin/ subdir appended
> # otherwise, leave this commented
> #TMPDIR="/tmp"
> ```

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
On systems with RAM (or zram) logging, which is naturally not boot-persistent unless separately rotated elsewhere, the dedicated file logging of Jellyfin itself is somewhat nonsense. It logs the very same to console=systemd-journald=syslog anyway. If a syslog daemon is installed, this is usually duplicated to `/var/log/syslog` and `/var/log/daemon.log`, and in any case accessible via `journalctl -u jellyfin`. On recent Debian/Ubuntu where `/var/log/journal` exists by default (not present in RAM logging cases, or that would be a misconfiguration), it is even boot-persistent.

Means: The dedicated Jellyfin file logging is pretty redundant, and it would make probably more sense to disable it by default. And in RAM logging cases these arguments weight stronger. But currently, with the embedded Serilog config, it is impossible to disable file logging, unless I am missing something.

I hence opened a feature request for this: https://<redacted-host>/posts/3537/add-option-to-disable-file-logging
When properly implemented, so that the logging dir size check us skipped if file logging is disabled, it would enable a much better way to solve this issue for RAM logging cases.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
@participant17 `/tmp` is not your issue, the log dir is:

> ```
> The path /var/log/jellyfin has insufficient free
> ```

You use Armbian or DietPi with RAM/tmpfs or zram `/var/log` mount? Check with:
```sh
df /var/log
```
EDIT: Ah looks like an image from Xunlong. However, they use an Armbian fork for their images, hence likely zram for `/var/log` by default.

You can move the log dir into the data dir:
```sh
sudo sed -i '/^JELLYFIN_LOG_DIR=/c\JELLYFIN_LOG_DIR=/var/lib/jellyfin/log' /etc/default/jellyfin
sudo systemctl restart jellyfin
```

Another option would be to raise the tmpfs/zram size to 512 MiB, but IMO it is not reasonable to allow such amounts of logs if a tmpfs/zram was chosen already.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Makes sense, Flatpak apps do not make use of the host's `/tmp`. Problematic for any kind of container. But you should have access to the config or env and set `TMPDIR` there as well, don't you?

I recognize something just now:
> insufficient **free space**

I have not really thought about it, but this means that Jallyfin can fail to restart because of its own produced data that is within the intended limits. E.g. it demands 512 MiB of free space for logs. In case of RAM logging, one adjusts the tmpfs size accordingly. Now Jellyfin starts logging up to a steady state with its internal rotation, hence free space falls below 512 MiB again. So even that 512 MiB is already an insane limit for log files, it demands an additional +512 MiB free space on top of what it actually uses.

In case of temporary files, it is expected that it cleans up those, at latest on restart. But generally the same can happen. In the systemd unit, this makes `PrivateTmp=true` sort of mandatory, to assure it cannot leave behind and choke on its own temporary data on a service restart.

The cache dir is probably the only one, where checking for a certain free space has more up than downsides, since transcoding is often used and requires significant amounts of space. But since the cache is more permanent than the temporary data (?), the problem of Jellyfin choking on its own cache data is probably even more likely. Maybe an idea to check this only once on first start, leaving some marker/flag, and no check it again. If things change, some migration can unset the marker.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
This is two bad advices:
- Do not clutter the root directory with temporary files, which implies a risk that it collides with essential system directories.
- Do not run a web facing service as root, which pulls in security risks, including unintentional overwrites or removals of any file with malicious symlinks, especially when you just told it to use `/` as base dir for temporary files (while I know it should use a `jellyfin/` subdir).

The space check has been removed, hence any action is obsolete and potentially harmful. Safe alternative paths, if `/tmp` is really too small (practically, not according to the removed arbitrary check), have been suggested, including `/var/tmp` and probably best for permission isolation: `TMPDIR="$JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR/tmp"` or `TMPDIR="$JELLYFIN_CACHE_DIR/tmp"`.
